title: InMoov Project: Teleoperated Robotic Arm with Flexible Sensor Glove

information.value: Personal Project - Presented at the Fête de la Science, Rouen 2023

Individual finger control via a glove equipped with flexible sensors / 2.4 GHz wireless communication (~50m range) / 8-hour autonomy with 18650 batteries / Charging via integrated BMS accessible from the surface / Displayed under a dome for exhibitions

Arduino Nano (arm and glove) / Flexible sensors / 2.4 GHz transmission / 18650 batteries (4 parallel packs of 2 cells in series - 7.4V) / SLS 3D printing (current version) / First version in white FDM 3D printing / Power bank for glove power supply / Integrated BMS with accessible charging port

description: This project is a redesign and improvement of the InMoov robotic arm, modified for presentation at the Fête de la Science in Rouen 2023. The main objective was to achieve smooth, individual control of each finger of the robotic arm through a connected glove.

The glove is equipped with flexible sensors that allow independent control of each finger. Data transmission occurs via a 2.4 GHz wireless link, providing a range of approximately 50 meters when the battery is fully charged.

The arm features 8 hours of autonomy, powered by 18650 batteries: four parallel packs, each consisting of two cells in series, providing approximately 7.4V. The glove is powered by a phone power bank, ensuring mobile and practical use.

The first version of the arm was made using FDM 3D printing (white). Currently, a new version is being produced using SLS 3D printing, offering better finish, robustness, and movement precision. The arm will be displayed under a dome, equipped with an integrated BMS and a surface-accessible charging port for easy presentation at exhibitions and shows.

This project allowed me to develop skills in mechatronics, embedded electronics, energy management, and advanced additive manufacturing, while exploring intuitive control techniques using flexible sensors.
